chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi said: Ubaydillah ibn Musa al-Royani narrated to us that Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Zayd ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood, who said: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) said regarding:
“Some faces, that Day, will be bright, looking at their Lord.”
He said: This means shining, awaiting the reward of their Lord.
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'nadirah' (bright faces) mean in the context of the Day of Judgment according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida elucidates the term 'nadirah' in Surah Qiyamah, interpreting it as faces that are radiant and illuminated by divine light. This exegesis highlights the spiritual state of the righteous who, purified from worldly darkness, gaze with anticipation and joy upon their Lord, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the beatific vision as the ultimate reward.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 11-2 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqqaq - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi quoted on the authority of Ubaydillah ibn Musa Al-Royani, on the authority of Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah ibn Ali ibn Al-Hassan ibn Zayd ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (s), on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmood, “Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (s) said the following regarding the Words of the Sublime God, ‘Some faces, that Day, will beam (in brightness and beauty) looking towards their Lord.’
This means that these faces will be shining awaiting the reward of their Lord.”
